messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions in German Democratic Republic (1949-1990) during the 1990s?
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

queries: East Germany GDR 1990 health survey dataset diseases morbidity Robert Koch
German Democratic Republic 1990s disease registry dataset cancer incidence eastern Germany
GESIS East Germany 1990 1991 health survey dataset illness
action.query: East Germany GDR 1990 health survey dataset diseases morbidity Robert Koch

queries: site:search.gesis.org/research_data "Specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions" "1990" "German Democratic Republic"
action.query: site:search.gesis.org/research_data "Specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions" "1990" "German Democratic Republic"

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Health 1990 (Gesundheit 1990)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.6379","justification":"Highly relevant dataset collected in June 1990 in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Covers health-related information from individuals aged 14 and older. Provides a historical source for examining population health around German reunification. Archived by GESIS Data Archive."},{"title":"Partners III – Employed Persons 1990 (Partner III – Berufstätige 1990)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.6142","justification":"Survey conducted in the GDR during the first half of 1990. Classified by GESIS under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions, particularly concerning HIV/AIDS, sexual behavior, reproductive health and disease-related awareness. Useful for researching public health attitudes and HIV/AIDS prevention in the final year of the GDR."},{"title":"Partners III – Apprentices 1990 (Partner III – Lehrlinge 1990)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.6146","justification":"Survey conducted in the GDR in 1990 examining relationships, sexuality and sexual behavior among young people during the AIDS epidemic. Classified under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions. Relevant for investigating HIV/AIDS awareness and sexual health risks among young East Germans."},{"title":"Nuclear Energy and Environmental Consciousness 1990 (Kernenergie und Umweltbewusstsein 1990)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.6578","justification":"Dataset based on a 1990 survey of 704 respondents across the five eastern German states. Classified by GESIS under specific diseases, disorders and medical conditions. Includes perceptions of health risks, environmental hazards and nuclear energy. Particularly useful for studying perceived environmental health threats in the former GDR, although it does not primarily measure diagnosed diseases."},{"title":"German General Social Survey (ALLBUS) – Cumulation 1980–2014","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.12574","justification":"Longitudinal collection of German population surveys, including eastern Germany beginning in 1991. Contains information about chronic illnesses, physical and psychological health, disabilities, healthcare utilization and HIV/AIDS awareness. The 1991–1998 survey waves are relevant for investigating disease-related conditions in the former GDR during the 1990s. Geographic identifiers enable East–West comparisons."},{"title":"System of Social Indicators for the Federal Republic of Germany: Health","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.14262","justification":"Historical health-indicator dataset covering Germany from 1950 to 2013, including the 1990s. Includes causes of death, ongoing illnesses, disabilities, sickness absence, medical treatment and medication use. Useful for examining historical changes in health conditions around reunification, subject to the availability of separate eastern German observations."},{"title":"Life in Eastern Germany 1992 (Leben Ostdeutschland 1992)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA6346","justification":"Population survey conducted in eastern Germany in 1992, shortly after the dissolution of the GDR. Includes questions concerning health, health-related lifestyles, social security and living conditions. Useful for contextualizing health and disease-related experiences during the transition from the GDR, although it is not primarily a clinical disease dataset."},{"title":"German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS) and Historical German Health Surveys","url_or_doi":"https://www.rki.de/EN/Topics/Noncommunicable-diseases/Health-surveys/Studies/DEGS/degs_content.html","justification":"Official Robert Koch Institute study landing page providing information about German population health surveys and their historical comparisons. Particularly relevant because the earlier Health Survey East was conducted in 1991–1992 among residents of the former GDR, while the nationwide 1998 survey included eastern German participants. The surveys cover cardiovascular conditions, chronic diseases, health risk factors and healthcare utilization. Historical microdata access may require contacting the Robert Koch Institute."},{"title":"German Cancer Registry Data – Epidemiological Cancer Statistics","url_or_doi":"https://www.healthinformationportal.eu/node/502","justification":"Dataset resource describing cancer incidence, mortality, prevalence and survival statistics from the German Centre for Cancer Registry Data. Its geographic and disease-specific indicators are relevant for investigating cancer patterns in eastern Germany following reunification. The listed resource begins in 1999, so its direct coverage of the earlier 1990s and historical GDR territory is limited."},{"title":"GESIS Microcensus Trendfile","url_or_doi":"https://www.gesis.org/en/gml/microcensus/microcensus-trendfile","justification":"Harmonized German microcensus data covering multiple decades, including 1991, 1993 and 1995–1999. Contains health-related variables and demographic information, potentially allowing analysis of residents of the former GDR after reunification. Useful for population-level studies of health inequalities and associated risk factors, although detailed disease-specific information may be limited."}]}
